correctness.rationale: The unit action on characters of the additive cyclic group has one orbit of each order p^k; the stabilizer in the cyclic complement is generated by b^φ(p^k). The explicit exhaustive character parametrization agrees with this little-groups construction. In a nonlinear representation of degree d=φ(p^k) the shift part first forces d|y for a^x b^y to be in the kernel. Comparing adjacent diagonal entries then forces p^k|x because the primitive multiplier r is not 1 mod p. The residual condition is ω^(y/d)=1. If ω has order p^s, the two independent divisibilities give kernel order p^(2(n−k)−s) and codegree p^(k+s). For fixed t=k+s, the nonlinear count telescopes to p^(t−1); linear characters contribute φ(p^t) below the top and nothing at p^n. For e>1 dividing p−1 the ep^s entries are entirely linear. The maximal codegree p^n strictly exceeds the largest possible linear codegree, and its multiplicity p^(n−1) yields p via their ratio and then n. The proof only claims rigidity within this family.
residual_risks: The packaged finite checker recycles the analytic kernel formula; it is a counting consistency check rather than an independent test of kernels. The symbolic proof suffices. The argument is not for p=2 or arbitrary groups.

originality.rationale: The complete codegree distribution is a direct extraction from the older exhaustive monomial representation table, not just a consequence of its degree multiset. Its entries are read off by testing when a cyclic shift is diagonal, comparing two diagonal entries, and reading the order of the scalar in the wrap-around slot. Grouping by k+s is the elementary totient sum. The rigidity assertion is immediate from the resulting maximal entry and adds no distinct group-theoretic input. This is mechanical prior implication, not evidence of a literally printed earlier codegree table.
residual_risks: Moretó's full text was not accessible. An earlier explicit codegree table could still exist; the rejection rests on the positively verified implication of the complete representation table.
